hook: *78%* of E. coli in Telangana blood samples resist a common antibiotic
hook_b: *78%* of E. coli in Telangana blood samples resist a common antibiotic
tldr: Osmania Medical College's TARS-Net report analysed 14,616 bacterial samples from 13 centres in 10 districts. It found high resistance to common antibiotics, and meropenem resistance in ICU Acinetobacter rising from 22% in 2024 to 47% in 2025.

beats.what: An OMC surveillance report shows common antibiotics failing against many infections in Telangana hospitals.
beats.why: Resistant bacteria leave doctors fewer options for critically ill patients.
beats.care: Experts say resistant bacteria are found even in people with no history of antibiotic use.

effects.label: Experts push state AMR plan TAPCAR

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: TOI (Nov 20): the report comes during World AMR Awareness Week, Nov 18-24.

cards.q: Do you take antibiotics only on a doctor's prescription?

qs: How often are antibiotics sold without prescription near you?
What happens when even last-line drugs stop working?

facts.t: The report analysed *14,616* bacterial samples; E. coli made up 5,716 of them.
Resistance to ceftriaxone was *74%* among E. coli found in urine samples.

viz.verdict: A powerful drug is failing more often in ICU infections
Four in five samples resisted this drug

learn.t: AMR = antimicrobial resistance, when germs stop responding to medicines meant to kill them

watch: Experts urged the state to implement its AMR containment plan (TAPCAR) across health, animals and farming.

sources.name: Times of India
sources.title: Powerful antibiotics losing effectiveness against infections in Telangana hospitals, states Osmania Medical College report

fact: Nearly *78%* of E. coli in Telangana patients' blood resisted ceftriaxone
twist: Resistance to meropenem, a last-line drug, nearly doubled in ICU Acinetobacter samples in a year.
